features.description: Make Jarvis pipx-installable with a global `jarvis` console script. Turn `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/` into a properly packaged Python distribution: add a top-level `pyproject.toml` (or extend the existing one) declaring `[project]` with name `jarvis-orchestrate`, runtime deps (pydantic, pyyaml, jsonschema, firebase-admin), and `[project.scripts] jarvis = "jarvis_orchestrate.cli:main"`. After `pipx install jarvis-orchestrate` (or `pipx install .` from the source tree), invoking `jarvis --help` from any cwd lists subcommands without requiring `PYTHONPATH=scripts`. Add `~/.jarvis/config.json` as global config with `default_implementer`, `default_auditor`, `default_tier`, optional `calibration_path`. The CLI loads it lazily and merges with any per-project override (F003). Existing `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan>` invocation keeps working — no flag-day break for the maintainer's own dogfood (D001). pipx (not pip) is the install path because Jarvis is a global tool, not a project dependency; pipx isolates Jarvis's own venv from any project venv (D002).
steps: Create or extend `pyproject.toml` at repo root: `[project]` with name=jarvis-orchestrate, version pulled from a single source of truth, python>=3.10, dependencies=[pydantic>=2, pyyaml, jsonschema, firebase-admin], `[project.scripts] jarvis = "jarvis_orchestrate.cli:main"`, `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["scripts"]`. Verify `pip install -e .` then `jarvis --help` works without `PYTHONPATH=`.
Verify pipx install path: `pipx install .` from a fresh shell, confirm `which jarvis` resolves to the pipx-managed binary, `jarvis ps` runs cleanly. Document this in README's quickstart.

Add `~/.jarvis/config.json` global-config loader at `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/global_config.py`: schema = `{default_implementer: str, default_auditor: str, default_tier: str | None, calibration_path: str | None}`, missing-file = empty dict (not error), invalid-JSON = WARNING + empty dict (don't block CLI startup). Pydantic-validated with `extra='forbid'`.

Wire global config into `cli._approve_main`, `cli._resume_main`, `dispatch-from-plan`, and `dispatch_volley` lookups so when no per-project override exists, defaults come from global config (instead of hardcoded 'claude' / 'codex'). Hardcoded fallbacks remain for empty-config case.
Update README quickstart to use `pipx install jarvis-orchestrate` as the canonical path; keep `pip install -e .` as the developer-mode alternative. Drop the `PYTHONPATH=scripts` prefixes throughout.

Tests: (a) packaging — `pyproject.toml` parses as valid PEP 621, `python -m build` produces a wheel, the wheel installs cleanly into a fresh venv. (b) console script — `jarvis --help` exits 0 from any cwd post-install. (c) global config — missing file returns empty defaults, invalid JSON warns and returns empty, valid file populates `default_implementer` / `default_auditor` correctly. (d) backward compat — `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan>` still works.
features.acceptance: (1) Repo has a top-level `pyproject.toml` valid per PEP 621 declaring the `jarvis` console script. (2) `pipx install .` from the source tree puts a `jarvis` binary on PATH that runs from any cwd. (3) `pip install -e .` (developer mode) works and supports test discovery. (5) Global config defaults flow into supervisor when no per-project override exists. (6) `python -m jarvis_orchestrate <plan>` still works (backward compat — no flag-day break per D001). (7) README quickstart uses pipx; `PYTHONPATH=scripts` removed from primary instructions. (8) All existing orchestrate-suite tests pass (~580 + 6 skipped baseline). (9) Ruff clean, sanitization clean.

features.description: Add project registry CRUD: `jarvis projects add | list | show | remove`. Registry lives at `~/.jarvis/projects.json` (global, single source of truth). Each entry: `name` (string, primary key), `path` (absolute), `created_at` (ISO timestamp), `last_used_at` (ISO timestamp, updated on dispatch), optional `default_implementer`, `default_auditor`, optional `notes`. Non-clobbering: `add` refuses if name exists with exit 2 + clear error; `add --force` requires interactive confirmation OR `--yes` flag for scripted use. `remove` requires `--yes` to actually delete (default is dry-run preview). `show <name>` prints the entry as readable JSON. `list` prints a tabular summary (name, path, last-used). All commands support `--json` for machine-readable output (agents reading via shell-out can parse). Project name pattern: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` (lowercase, hyphen-separated, no underscores, max 64 chars) to avoid filename / URL ambiguity. Path is `Path.expanduser().resolve()`-normalized at add time (operator can add with `~/...`; registry stores absolute).
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/projects_registry.py` with Pydantic model `ProjectEntry`: `name: str` (regex-validated), `path: str` (validated as existing dir at add time), `created_at: str`, `last_used_at: str | None`, `default_implementer: str | None`, `default_auditor: str | None`, `notes: str | None`. `Registry` model wraps `projects: list[ProjectEntry]`. Functions: `load_registry() -> Registry` (missing file → empty), `save_registry(reg)`, `add_project(name, path, **kwargs)` (refuses on dup), `remove_project(name)`, `find_project(name) -> ProjectEntry | None`, `update_last_used(name)`.

Add CLI subcommands in `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/cli.py`: `_projects_main(argv)` dispatches `add | list | show | remove` to handlers. Each handler supports `--json` flag. `add` flags: `--force`, `--yes`, optional `--implementer`, `--auditor`, `--notes`. `remove` requires `--yes` (default is dry-run preview).

Wire `--json` output across all four subcommands so agents shelling out can parse. `list --json` returns `{"projects": [...]}`; `show --json` returns the single entry; `add` / `remove` return `{"action": "...", "project": {...}}`.

Tests: (a) `add` with valid name + existing path persists to `~/.jarvis/projects.json` (use a per-test override env var `JARVIS_REGISTRY_PATH`). (b) `add` with name collision exits 2; `--force --yes` overwrites. (c) `add` with invalid name (uppercase / underscore / >64 chars) exits 2 with regex hint. (d) `add` with non-existent path exits 2. (e) `remove` without `--yes` is dry-run; with `--yes` deletes. (f) `list` and `show --json` round-trip without dropping fields. (g) `update_last_used` mutates the field; idempotent within the same second.
features.acceptance: (1) `jarvis projects add foo /path/to/foo` writes `~/.jarvis/projects.json` with a well-formed entry (name, absolute path, created_at, optional defaults). (2) `jarvis projects add foo …` a second time exits 2 with a clear collision message; `--force --yes` overwrites. (3) `jarvis projects list` prints a table; `jarvis projects list --json` is parseable. (4) `jarvis projects show foo` and `--json` round-trip all fields. (5) `jarvis projects remove foo` is dry-run by default; `--yes` deletes. (6) Project name regex `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$` enforced; non-existent paths refused. (7) `~/.jarvis/projects.json` shape: `{"projects": [{...}, ...]}`; missing file = empty registry (not error). (8) All new tests pass. Ruff + sanitization clean.

features.description:
Per-project config at `<project>/.jarvis/jarvis.json` (committable; lives inside the registered project, not in `~/.jarvis/`). Schema: `{implementer: str | null, auditor: str | null, plans_dir: str (default 'docs/plans'), default_target_env: str (default 'dev'), human_gates: list[str] | null, protected_paths: list[str] | null}`. Per-project values override global config (F001) override hardcoded fallbacks. Also: extend the existing `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py` to check global + per-project config when a project is registered: (a) `~/.jarvis/config.json` parses if present; (b) for each registered project: path exists, `.jarvis/jarvis.json` parses if present, declared `plans_dir` exists or is creatable, declared agents are recognized by AGENT_REGISTRY, declared `human_gates` are valid gate names. Doctor exit code: 0 if all PASS, 1 if any WARN, 2 if any FAIL. `jarvis doctor` (the new console-script subcommand) wraps the existing `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py` so users get one entry point. The supervisor lookup chain becomes: per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json` > global `~/.jarvis/config.json` > hardcoded defaults.

## Operator audit-focus addendum (review priorities, not new ACs)

Required reading before implementing OR auditing this feature: `docs/plans/2026-05-03-001-feat-global-install-project-registry/evidence/f002-closeout-memo.md` (F003 wiring checklist + concrete audit focus areas, recorded by the operator at F002 close-out).

The acceptance items above are the binding contract. The list below is operator-supplied review priorities — areas where past dispatch-path bugs have hidden and where the auditor must touch on each item explicitly in their findings paragraph (PASS/CONCERN/FAIL on each, not silence). These do NOT add new acceptance items; they sharpen the auditor's beam:

1. **Missed call sites.** The override-resolution helper must be threaded into every code path that today reads `agents_required[0]` / `agents_required[1]` or hardcodes `'claude'` / `'codex'` — not just the obvious ones in `dispatch_volley`. Implementer must grep `supervisor.py` and `cli.py` for both shapes; auditor must independently re-grep and verify nothing was missed.
2. **Wrong precedence.** Per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json` must win over global `~/.jarvis/config.json` must win over hardcoded fallbacks (per D004). A bug where global wins when both are set is a silent drift bug. The test must cover all four cells of (per-project set/unset × global set/unset), not just the happy path.
3. **Unsafe fallback to cwd.** Project resolution must never default to `Path.cwd()` — that's how Jarvis ends up operating on the wrong repo. A missing or unregistered project name is a HARD REFUSAL with exit 2 + clear message, not a silent cwd fallback. Auditor must search the diff for any `Path.cwd()` introductions in the resolution path.
4. **Project name vs project path confusion.** The CLI accepts both shapes (`jarvis dispatch myproject` vs `jarvis dispatch /abs/path/to/proj`). The override-resolution helper must not treat a name as a path or vice versa. Tests must cover both shapes and an ambiguous-input case (e.g., a relative-path-shaped string that also matches a project name pattern).
5. **None vs missing config values.** Per-project `default_implementer: null` in JSON has two possible meanings — (a) explicit override to None / (b) no override, fall through to global. Pick ONE meaning, document it in the resolver's docstring, and test both interpretations are not silently conflated. Pydantic's default behavior must be pinned by a test — don't trust framework default semantics across versions.
6. **Tests that only cover happy path.** Edge cases that must have parametric coverage: per-project file missing, per-project file invalid JSON (degrades to global), per-project file with extra fields (Pydantic `extra='forbid'` rejects → degrades to global with WARN), conflicting per-project + global values (per-project wins), all-None values across both layers (fallback wins), unknown agent name in per-project (resolver refuses or warns — pick one, test it).
7. **approve/resume path behavior, not just dispatch.** `cli._approve_main` and `cli._resume_main` need the same precedence resolution when they emit messages or check whether a clearance applies. Today they hardcode the fallback; F003 must thread the resolver in. Auditor must walk approve/resume code paths in addition to dispatch_volley/dispatch_single_agent.
8. **Doctor behavior under project context.** `jarvis doctor` must surface concrete failures per registered project: path missing → FAIL with which path, jarvis.json invalid → FAIL with line/field, declared agent not in registry → FAIL with name, declared gate not valid → FAIL with name. Empty registry should not produce false-positive PASS — test the zero-state explicitly. Exit code matrix (0 all PASS / 1 any WARN / 2 any FAIL) must be parametric-tested.
steps: Add `scripts/jarvis_orchestrate/project_config.py` with Pydantic `ProjectConfig` model + `load_project_config(project_path: Path) -> ProjectConfig | None` (missing = None, invalid = warn + None). Cross-validation: `human_gates` must intersect known gate names from `gate_pause` module; `protected_paths` must be a list of strings.

Update `plan_loader.load()` to accept an optional override path for plans_dir (today it's hardcoded relative-to-cwd `docs/plans`). When a project is registered AND its config sets `plans_dir`, use that.

Update agent-resolution in `supervisor.dispatch_volley` and `dispatch_single_agent` to consult: (1) per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json`, (2) `~/.jarvis/config.json`, (3) hardcoded fallbacks. Test that override precedence is correct.

Wrap `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py` as a `jarvis doctor` subcommand. Add per-project checks: for each entry in `~/.jarvis/projects.json`, run path-exists + jarvis.json-parses + plans-dir-exists + agents-recognized + gates-valid. Output structured PASS/WARN/FAIL per check; non-zero exit when any FAIL.
Update `jarvis projects add` (F002) to optionally scaffold an empty `<project>/.jarvis/jarvis.json` (only when `--init-config` is passed; default is no scaffold to avoid surprise).

Tests: (a) per-project config loads + overrides global. (b) `jarvis doctor` with a registered project, no jarvis.json present → reports OK (config is optional). (c) `jarvis doctor` with invalid jarvis.json → FAIL with line/field detail. (d) `jarvis doctor` with declared plans_dir that doesn't exist → WARN. (e) override precedence: per-project > global > fallback verified by parametric test.
features.acceptance: (1) Per-project `.jarvis/jarvis.json` validates + loads; missing is OK (config is optional); invalid is WARN, not FAIL. (2) Override precedence at dispatch time: per-project > global (~/.jarvis/config.json) > hardcoded ('claude' / 'codex'). (3) `jarvis doctor` runs global preflight + per-registered-project preflight; outputs structured PASS / WARN / FAIL; non-zero exit on any FAIL. (4) `jarvis projects add --init-config` scaffolds an empty per-project config; default behavior is no scaffold. (5) Existing `scripts/jarvis_doctor.py` invocation unchanged (backward compat). (6) plan_loader respects per-project `plans_dir` when set. (7) All new tests pass. Ruff + sanitization clean. Full orchestrate suite still green.
